description: I'm a Game Development & Computer Science student building a mission simulator for this challenge. Players will manage a Moon or Mars outpost, balancing power, life support, radiation protection, and food production. I'm starting solo and looking to form a committed team. I can contribute Unity/C# development and gameplay design. Looking for teammates in programming, UI/UX, 2D/3D art, space/STEM research, or educational storytelling. Beginners ready to learn and build are welcome.
summary:
ARES-6 is a browser-based 2D Mars outpost mission trainer designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of human exploration of Mars.

Players manage a crew of four astronauts across seven Martian sols, balancing power, water, and food while inspecting facilities, responding to unexpected mission events, and completing scientific research objectives. Every decision has consequences, teaching players about resource management, problem-solving, and mission planning.

To connect gameplay with real space science, ARES-6 incorporates historical radiation observations from NASA's Curiosity rover and retrieves recent Solar Energetic Particle notifications through NASA's Community Coordinated Modeling Center (CCMC) DONKI system.

By combining interactive gameplay with real NASA resources, ARES-6 makes the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars more accessible, engaging, and educational for the next generation of space explorers.
details:
ARES-6 is an interactive, browser-based Mars outpost management game built around a seven-Sol survival mission.

Players are responsible for four astronauts and must manage three essential resources: power, water, and food. Each Sol introduces a mission event with decisions that can affect available resources, facility conditions, crew status, and research progress.

The outpost contains six interactive facilities: a habitat, solar array, greenhouse, storm shelter, communications antenna, and science rover. Players can inspect these facilities, monitor their status, respond to mission challenges, and work towards geological and environmental research objectives.

ARES-6 also includes a science information panel. It presents historical radiation observations recorded by the Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) aboard NASA's Curiosity rover. A separate panel retrieves recent Solar Energetic Particle notifications from NASA's DONKI service when available. These resources provide scientific context rather than direct predictions of the game's fictional outpost conditions.

The project aims to encourage curiosity about Mars exploration while introducing young learners to resource management, scientific research, risk awareness, and decision-making.

The game was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with JavaScript ES modules. Vite was used as the development and build tool. JSON files store the local scientific data and mission events. The NASA DONKI integration uses the browser Fetch API, with caching and error handling to support the application.

The project combines a clickable 2D outpost map, event-driven decisions, resource simulations, and NASA science information in one educational experience. Key design considerations included age-appropriate explanations, simple interactions, clear feedback, scientific accuracy, and keeping the simulation understandable without presenting fictional gameplay values as real mission measurements.
